source: Official government websites, PIB press releases, scheme guidelines

schemes.name: PM-KISAN
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi
schemes.whatItIs: Direct income support scheme for farmer families. Government transfers Rs 6,000 per year in three equal installments directly to the bank accounts of eligible farmer families.
benefits: Rs 6,000 per year (Rs 2,000 x 3 installments)
Direct bank transfer (DBT) to beneficiary account
Installments: Apr-Jul, Aug-Nov, Dec-Mar

whoCanApply: All land-holding farmer families across the country
Family defined as husband, wife, and minor children
Must have cultivable land in their name
whoCannotApply: Institutional land holders
Former and present holders of constitutional posts
Former and present Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, Mayors, Zila Parishad Chairpersons
Central/State government employees (except Multi-Tasking Staff, Class IV, Group D)
Superannuated/retired pensioners with monthly pension of Rs 10,000 or more
Income tax payers in the last assessment year
Professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, architects registered with professional bodies

documentsRequired: eKYC completion (OTP-based or biometric at CSC)
howToApply: Online: Self-registration at pmkisan.gov.in
CSC: Visit nearest Common Service Centre
Offline: Through local Patwari / Revenue Officer / Nodal Officer
State agriculture department offices
schemes.grievance: File complaint on pmkisan.gov.in helpdesk or contact district agriculture officer

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (Ayushman Bharat)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / National Health Authority
schemes.whatItIs: World's largest government-funded health insurance scheme providing Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization at empanelled hospitals across India.
benefits: Rs 5,00,000 health cover per family per year
Cashless and paperless treatment at empanelled hospitals
Covers 1,929+ medical procedures including surgery, diagnostics, medicines
Pre-existing conditions covered from day one
3 days pre-hospitalization and 15 days post-hospitalization expenses covered
No restriction on family size, age, or gender
Portable across India - use at any empanelled hospital
Ayushman Vay Vandana card for citizens 70+ (additional coverage)

whoCanApply: Families identified via SECC 2011 (Socio-Economic Caste Census) database
Rural: Households meeting deprivation criteria (D1-D5, D7) - kucha house, no adult earning member, female-headed household, SC/ST, landless manual laborers, destitute/living on alms, bonded labor

Urban: 11 occupational categories - ragpickers, street vendors, domestic workers, construction workers, plumbers, painters, welders, security guards, coolies, sweepers, sanitation workers, transport workers, shop workers, rickshaw pullers, electricians, mechanics, washermen
All RSBY (Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana) beneficiary families
Citizens aged 70+ (added in 2024) regardless of income
whoCannotApply: Families not listed in SECC 2011 database (unless 70+)
Those with other government health insurance (CGHS/ECHS) - though 70+ can get additional top-up

documentsRequired: SECC database match (checked at point of care)
Any government photo ID if Aadhaar unavailable
howToApply: No advance enrollment needed - entitlement based
Check eligibility: beneficiary.nha.gov.in or call 14555
Get Ayushman Card: Download Ayushman App and complete e-KYC
Visit any empanelled hospital - they verify eligibility on the spot
CSC centres can also help create Ayushman Card
schemes.grievance: Online: cgrms.nha.gov.in | Phone: 14555 | Resolution within 30 days

schemes.name: MGNREGA
schemes.fullName: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
schemes.whatItIs: Legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment per year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. It is a demand-driven scheme - work must be provided within 15 days of demand, failing which an unemployment allowance is payable.
benefits: 100 days guaranteed wage employment per household per year
Wage rate: State-specific (Rs 230-350/day depending on state, revised annually)
Wages paid within 15 days via Direct Benefit Transfer
Unemployment allowance if work not provided within 15 days of demand
Worksite facilities: drinking water, shade, first-aid, creche for children
Work provided within 5 km of residence; extra 10% wages if beyond
One-third of beneficiaries must be women

whoCanApply: Any adult member of a rural household
Willing to do unskilled manual work
Must reside in rural area (notified Gram Panchayat)
No income or land-holding restriction
Must obtain a Job Card from Gram Panchayat
whoCannotApply: Urban residents (urban areas not covered)
Those unwilling to do manual/physical labor

documentsRequired: Proof of residence in the Gram Panchayat
howToApply: Apply at Gram Panchayat office for Job Card (free of cost)
Job Card issued within 15 days of application
Submit written application demanding work (keep receipt)
Work must be provided within 15 days of demand
Online: nrega.nic.in for status tracking

stateHelplines.note: Other states: contact District Programme Coordinator or visit nrega.nic.in for state-specific numbers

schemes.grievance: Complain to Programme Officer → District Programme Coordinator → State government → Central government. Social Audit by Gram Sabha mandatory every 6 months.

schemes.name: PM Awas Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Housing for All)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (Urban) / Ministry of Rural Development (Gramin)
schemes.whatItIs: Affordable housing scheme providing financial assistance for construction or purchase of houses for eligible families. Two components: PMAY-Urban for cities and PMAY-Gramin (PMAY-G) for rural areas.
benefits: PMAY-Urban: Interest subsidy of 3-6.5% on home loans under CLSS component
PMAY-Urban EWS/LIG: Subsidy up to Rs 2.67 lakh on loans up to Rs 6 lakh
PMAY-Urban MIG-I: Subsidy up to Rs 2.35 lakh on loans up to Rs 9 lakh
PMAY-Urban MIG-II: Subsidy up to Rs 2.30 lakh on loans up to Rs 12 lakh
PMAY-Gramin: Rs 1.20 lakh (plains) / Rs 1.30 lakh (hilly/difficult areas) for house construction
PMAY-Gramin: Additional Rs 12,000 for toilet under SBM
90/95 days of MGNREGA wages for unskilled labor in construction

whoCanApply: PMAY-Urban EWS: Annual household income up to Rs 3 lakh
PMAY-Urban LIG: Annual household income Rs 3-6 lakh
PMAY-Urban MIG-I: Annual household income Rs 6-12 lakh
PMAY-Urban MIG-II: Annual household income Rs 12-18 lakh
PMAY-Gramin: Identified from SECC 2011 data, verified by Gram Sabha
Beneficiary family should not own a pucca house anywhere in India
Women ownership/co-ownership mandatory for EWS/LIG (except for urban CLSS)
whoCannotApply: Families already owning a pucca house anywhere in India
Previous beneficiaries of government housing schemes
Government employees (for EWS/LIG categories)

documentsRequired: Aadhaar card of all family members
Proof of not owning a pucca house (self-declaration)
Land documents (for construction on own land)
howToApply: PMAY-Urban: Online at pmaymis.gov.in
PMAY-Urban: Through banks/HFCs for CLSS subsidy on home loans
PMAY-Urban: CSC centres for online application
PMAY-Gramin: Through Gram Panchayat (beneficiary selection by Gram Sabha)
PMAY-Gramin: Identified from Awaas+ survey / SECC data
schemes.grievance: Online at PMAY MIS portal or contact Urban Local Body / District office

schemes.name: PM Ujjwala Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
schemes.whatItIs: Provides free LPG connections to women from below poverty line (BPL) and other deprived households to replace unclean cooking fuels like wood, cow dung, and coal, reducing indoor air pollution and health hazards.
benefits: Free LPG connection (security deposit for cylinder + regulator waived)
Financial assistance of Rs 1,600 per connection
Option for EMI on cost of stove and first refill
First LPG refill and stove provided free under Ujjwala 2.0
Subsidy on subsequent LPG refills via DBT
Up to 12 subsidized cylinders per year

whoCanApply: Adult woman from a BPL household
No existing LPG connection in the household from any oil company
Ujjwala 2.0: Migrant workers' families, no address proof needed (self-declaration)
Priority: SC/ST households, PMAY beneficiaries, Antyodaya Anna Yojana, forest dwellers, most backward classes, tea/ex-tea garden tribes, people in islands/river islands
whoCannotApply: Households already having an LPG connection
Applicant must be a woman (male members cannot apply)

documentsRequired: BPL card / ration card / SECC identification
Self-declaration of not having LPG connection (Ujjwala 2.0)
Address proof (Ujjwala 2.0 accepts self-declaration for migrants)
howToApply: Visit nearest LPG distributor (Indane/HP Gas/Bharat Gas)
Fill Ujjwala application form (KYC form)
Online: pmuy.gov.in for application
Contact OMC customer care for nearest distributor
schemes.checkStatus: Through respective OMC portals (Indane/HP Gas/Bharat Gas)
schemes.grievance: LPG helpline 1906 or contact district nodal officer

schemes.name: PM Jan Dhan Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance / Department of Financial Services
schemes.whatItIs: National mission for financial inclusion ensuring access to financial services like banking, credit, insurance, and pension for every household in the country. Provides zero-balance bank accounts with a RuPay debit card and insurance cover.
benefits: Zero-balance savings account at any bank
Free RuPay debit card with Rs 2 lakh accident insurance
Life insurance cover of Rs 30,000 (for accounts opened before Jan 2015)
Overdraft facility up to Rs 10,000 (after 6 months satisfactory operation)
Mobile banking facility
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of government subsidies to this account
No minimum balance requirement
Interest on deposits

whoCanApply: Any Indian citizen aged 10 years or above
Those who do not have any existing bank account (or can convert existing basic account)
Minor accounts (10-18 years) can be opened jointly with guardian
whoCannotApply: Only one account per person (no duplicate accounts allowed)
NRIs (Non-Resident Indians) are not eligible
Existing holders of a savings account at any bank can convert to PMJDY but cannot open a second PMJDY account
Joint accounts are not allowed under PMJDY (must be individual)

documentsRequired: Aadhaar card (if available, no other document needed)
If Aadhaar not available: Voter ID / Driving License / PAN / Passport / MGNREGA Job Card
If no officially valid documents: Letter from Gazetted Officer with photograph
howToApply: Visit any bank branch (public or private sector)
Visit Banking Correspondent (BC) agents in villages
Fill simplified account opening form
Online through some bank websites
schemes.grievance: Banking Ombudsman (RBI) at cms.rbi.org.in or bank grievance cell

schemes.name: PM Mudra Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency)
schemes.whatItIs: Provides loans up to Rs 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises for income-generating activities. Three categories based on business stage: Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun.
benefits: Shishu: Loans up to Rs 50,000 (for startup stage businesses)
Kishore: Loans from Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000 (for mid-stage businesses)
Tarun: Loans from Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 10,00,000 (for growth stage businesses)
No collateral or guarantor required
No processing fee on Shishu loans
Mudra Card for working capital management
Repayment period: Up to 5-7 years

whoCanApply: Any Indian citizen with a business plan for non-farm income-generating activity
Small/micro manufacturing, trading, services, or allied agriculture enterprises
Shopkeepers, vendors, artisans, food service providers
Existing businesses needing expansion capital
Individuals, partnership firms, or proprietary concerns
whoCannotApply: Corporate entities
Farm/agriculture activities (covered under separate schemes)
Loan amounts above Rs 10 lakh

documentsRequired: Identity proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / PAN / Passport)
Proof of business existence (GST, Udyam registration, license, etc.)
Last 6 months bank statement (for existing businesses)
howToApply: Visit any bank branch (public, private, small finance, RRB)
Apply through Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs)
Online: udyamimitra.in for Mudra loan applications
Through NBFCs registered with MUDRA
Jan Dhan account holders can apply at their bank
schemes.grievance: Contact lending bank grievance cell → Banking Ombudsman (RBI)

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
schemes.fullName: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (Girl Child Savings Scheme)
schemes.whatItIs: Small deposit savings scheme for the girl child under the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' campaign. Offers one of the highest interest rates among government savings instruments with tax benefits.
benefits: Interest rate: ~8.2% per annum (revised quarterly by government)
Tax benefit: Investment up to Rs 1.5 lakh/year under Section 80C
Tax-free interest and maturity amount (EEE status)
Maturity: 21 years from account opening or marriage after age 18
Partial withdrawal: Up to 50% after girl turns 18 (for education/marriage)
Minimum deposit: Rs 250/year
Maximum deposit: Rs 1,50,000/year
Deposits required for first 15 years only; interest accrues for remaining 6 years

whoCanApply: Parent/legal guardian of a girl child below 10 years
Maximum 2 accounts (one per girl child, max 2 daughters)
Exception: Third account allowed in case of twins/triplets
Girl child must be an Indian resident
whoCannotApply: Girl child aged 10 or above at time of account opening
NRI (Non-Resident Indian) girl children
More than 2 accounts per family (except twins/triplets)

documentsRequired: Birth certificate of the girl child
Identity proof of parent/guardian (Aadhaar / PAN / Passport)
Passport-size photographs of parent and child
Medical certificate in case of twins/triplets (for third account)
howToApply: Visit any post office or authorized bank branch
Fill account opening form (SSA-1)
Submit documents and initial deposit (min Rs 250)
Banks: SBI, PNB, BOB, Canara Bank, ICICI, Axis, HDFC, etc.

helpline.email: Via respective bank or post office complaint portal

schemes.checkStatus: Passbook at post office / bank branch / India Post net banking (ippbonline.com) / IPPB app
schemes.grievance: Post office: Chief Postmaster General (dop.gov.in) | Bank: Banking Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in) | Escalate to NSIINDIA helpline

schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana
schemes.fullName: Atal Pension Yojana
schemes.whatItIs: Guaranteed minimum pension scheme for workers in the unorganized sector. Subscribers receive fixed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 after age 60, based on contribution amount and joining age.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension: Rs 1,000 / Rs 2,000 / Rs 3,000 / Rs 4,000 / Rs 5,000
Pension starts at age 60 and continues for life
After subscriber's death: Same pension to spouse for life
After both deaths: Corpus returned to nominee
Government co-contributed 50% of premium for first 5 years (for those who joined before Mar 2016 and are not taxpayers)
Example: Age 18, Rs 5,000 pension → contribute Rs 210/month

whoCanApply: Indian citizen aged 18-40 years
Must have a savings bank account
Must have a valid mobile number
Must not be an income tax payer (for government co-contribution)
whoCannotApply: Below 18 or above 40 years of age
Existing members of any statutory social security scheme (EPF/EPS/NPS-govt)
Income tax payers (can join but no government co-contribution)

documentsRequired: Mobile number linked to bank account
howToApply: Visit bank branch where savings account is held
Fill APY registration form or use net banking/mobile banking
Online: enps.nsdl.com for APY enrollment
Banks auto-debit monthly contribution from savings account
schemes.checkStatus: Net banking / APY mobile app / bank statement
schemes.grievance: PFRDA grievance portal or contact bank

schemes.name: PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
schemes.whatItIs: Affordable life insurance scheme offering Rs 2 lakh death cover (any cause) for just Rs 436/year premium. Renewable annually, available through bank accounts.
benefits: Life insurance cover: Rs 2,00,000
Covers death due to any reason
Annual premium: Rs 436 (auto-debited from bank account)
Renewable every year (June 1 to May 31)
No medical examination required

whoCanApply: Indian citizen aged 18-55 years
Must have a savings bank account
Must give consent for auto-debit of premium
Aadhaar linked to bank account
whoCannotApply: Below 18 or above 55 years at time of enrollment
Those without a bank account

howToApply: Visit bank branch and fill enrollment form
Enable via net banking / mobile banking
SMS-based enrollment (bank-specific)
Premium of Rs 436 auto-debited annually

helpline.email: Via bank insurance department or jansuraksha.gov.in contact form

schemes.checkStatus: Bank passbook / net banking / contact bank for active policy confirmation
schemes.grievance: Contact bank branch manager → Life Insurance Company (LIC/SBI Life/etc.) → IRDAI Grievance Portal (igms.irda.gov.in) or call 155255

schemes.name: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana
schemes.whatItIs: Cheapest accident insurance in the world. Rs 2 lakh for accidental death, Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for just Rs 20/year premium. Available to all bank account holders.
benefits: Accidental death cover: Rs 2,00,000
Permanent total disability: Rs 2,00,000
Permanent partial disability: Rs 1,00,000
Annual premium: Just Rs 20 (auto-debited from bank account)
Coverage period: June 1 to May 31 each year

whoCanApply: Indian citizen aged 18-70 years
Must have a savings bank account
Must give auto-debit consent for Rs 20/year
whoCannotApply: Below 18 or above 70 years
Those without a bank account

howToApply: Visit bank branch and fill one-page form
Enable via net banking / mobile banking
SMS-based enrollment (bank-specific)
Rs 20 auto-debited once a year from bank account

helpline.email: Via bank insurance department or jansuraksha.gov.in contact form

schemes.checkStatus: Bank passbook / net banking / contact bank for active policy confirmation
schemes.grievance: Contact bank branch manager → General Insurance Company → IRDAI Grievance Portal (igms.irda.gov.in) or call 155255

schemes.name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
schemes.whatItIs: Crop insurance scheme protecting farmers against crop loss due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases. Very low farmer premium (1.5-5% of sum insured), with remaining premium paid by government.
benefits: Kharif crops: Farmer pays only 2% of sum insured (e.g., Rs 900 premium on Rs 45,000 sum insured for paddy)
Rabi crops: Farmer pays only 1.5% of sum insured (e.g., Rs 750 premium on Rs 50,000 sum insured for wheat)
Commercial/horticultural crops: Farmer pays 5% of sum insured
Remaining premium paid by Central + State government (50:50)
No cap on government subsidy - full claim amount paid to farmer (average claim payout Rs 10,000-30,000 per farmer)
Sum insured: Rs 30,000-1,50,000 per hectare depending on crop and district (set by District Level Technical Committee)
Covers natural calamities, pests, diseases, post-harvest losses (14 days)
Add-on: Prevented sowing/planting cover, localized calamity cover
Claims settled within 2 months of harvest via DBT to bank account

whoCanApply: All farmers (landowners, tenant, sharecroppers)
Voluntary for all farmers (made voluntary from 2020)
Must be growing notified crops in notified areas
Loanee farmers: Can opt-out by declaration to bank
whoCannotApply: Non-notified crops or non-notified areas for the season
Farmers who miss the enrollment deadline for the crop season (strict cut-off dates)
Crops grown on unapproved / unauthorized land

documentsRequired: Land records (Khasra / Khatauni / land lease agreement)
Sowing certificate from Patwari / Revenue Officer
howToApply: Through bank branch (for loanee farmers, auto-enrolled with opt-out option)
Online: pmfby.gov.in for non-loanee farmers
CSC centres for enrollment
Through crop insurance companies
Deadline: Before cut-off date for each crop season
schemes.grievance: District agriculture officer → State agriculture department → Insurance company

schemes.name: National Scholarship Portal
schemes.fullName: National Scholarship Portal (NSP)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Electronics & IT (platform) / Various ministries (scholarships)
schemes.whatItIs: One-stop platform for multiple central and state government scholarships covering pre-matric, post-matric, merit-based, and means-based scholarships. Over 100 scholarship schemes from 30+ departments.
benefits: Pre-matric scholarships: Rs 1,000-6,000/year for classes 1-10
Post-matric scholarships: Rs 5,000-25,000/year for classes 11+, UG, PG
Merit-cum-means scholarships for professional courses
Minority community scholarships (Pre-matric, Post-matric, Merit-cum-Means)
SC/ST/OBC/EBC specific scholarships
Scholarships for persons with disabilities
Central Sector Scheme: Rs 10,000-20,000/year for top percentile students
All disbursement via Direct Benefit Transfer to bank account

whoCanApply: Indian students enrolled in recognized institutions
Eligibility varies by scholarship: income ceiling, caste category, merit percentage, domicile state
Common requirement: Family income typically below Rs 2-8 lakh/year (varies by scheme)
Must not be receiving any other scholarship simultaneously (for most schemes)
whoCannotApply: Students already receiving another government scholarship (usually)
Students in unrecognized institutions
Those exceeding income ceiling for the specific scholarship

documentsRequired: Bank account details (student's own or linked to Aadhaar)
howToApply: Register at scholarships.gov.in with Aadhaar
Complete One-Time Registration
Browse and apply for eligible scholarships
Institute verifies application → District verifies → State verifies → Disbursement
Apply during scholarship window (typically Jul-Nov for fresh, Mar-Apr for renewal)
schemes.grievance: NSP helpdesk → State nodal officer → Ministry concerned

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Vishwakarma Yojana
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
schemes.whatItIs: End-to-end support for traditional artisans and craftsmen through recognition, skill training, toolkit incentive, credit support, and market linkage. Covers 18 traditional trades.
benefits: PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card for recognition
Skill training: 5-7 days basic + 15 days advanced, with Rs 500/day stipend
Toolkit incentive: Rs 15,000 (e-voucher for trade-specific modern tools)
Credit: Collateral-free loans - Rs 1 lakh (first tranche) + Rs 2 lakh (second tranche)
Interest subvention: 5% subsidy, effective rate ~8% to beneficiary
Digital incentive: Rs 1 per transaction for digital payments (max Rs 100/month)
Marketing support: National Urban Livelihood Mission / GeM onboarding
Total support per beneficiary: Up to Rs 3 lakh+ over scheme period

whoCanApply: Artisans/craftsmen working in one of 18 specified trades

18 trades: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Blacksmith, Hammer & Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor, Cobbler, Mason, Basket/Mat Maker, Doll/Toy Maker, Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor, Fishing Net Maker
Must be working with hands and tools in traditional/self-employment capacity
Aged 18 years or above
Should not be in organized sector / government employment
Registration through Gram Panchayat / ULB verification
whoCannotApply: Those not engaged in the 18 specified trades
Government/PSU employees
Family members already registered under the scheme (one person per trade per family)

documentsRequired: Gram Panchayat / ULB verification of trade
howToApply: Visit CSC or camp organized by district administration
Online: pmvishwakarma.gov.in (registration with Aadhaar OTP)
Gram Panchayat / ULB verifies the artisan's trade
After verification: skill training → toolkit → credit in phases
schemes.grievance: Portal grievance section → District Task Force → State Task Force

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi
schemes.whatItIs: Micro-credit scheme for street vendors to restart businesses post-COVID. Provides collateral-free working capital loans with interest subsidy and cashback on digital transactions.
benefits: First loan: Rs 10,000 (repay in 1 year)
Second loan: Rs 20,000 (on timely repayment of first)
Third loan: Rs 50,000 (on timely repayment of second)
Interest subsidy: 7% per annum
Cashback: Up to Rs 1,200/year on digital transactions (UPI/BHIM/etc.)
No collateral or guarantor required
Builds formal credit history for vendor

whoCanApply: Street vendors with Certificate of Vending / Letter of Recommendation from ULB
Vendors identified in survey conducted by ULB
Vendors who were operating on or before March 24, 2020
Vendors in urban areas (all ULBs covered)
whoCannotApply: Rural vendors (not covered under this scheme)
Vendors without ULB identification/survey record

documentsRequired: Certificate of Vending or Letter of Recommendation from ULB/Town Vending Committee
howToApply: Online: pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in
Through lending institutions (banks, NBFCs, MFIs)
ULB/Municipal Corporation office
CSC centres
schemes.grievance: Portal grievance section → ULB → State Mission Director

schemes.name: DigiLocker
schemes.fullName: DigiLocker (Digital India / National Digital Locker System)
schemes.whatItIs: Cloud-based platform for issuance, storage, and verification of official documents and certificates. Provides citizens a digital document wallet linked to Aadhaar, eliminating the need for physical documents. Over 500 crore documents issued, 30 crore+ registered users.
benefits: Completely free service - no charges for storage, access, or sharing
Legally equivalent to original documents (under IT Act Section 9, Rule 9A)
Documents issued directly by government agencies to your locker (auto-fetched)
Supported documents: Aadhaar, PAN, driving license, vehicle RC, Class 10/12 marksheets, degree certificates, insurance policies, EPFO passbook
Accepted for KYC and verification at banks, airports, government offices, traffic police
1 GB free storage for uploaded personal documents (photos of certificates, etc.)
Share documents digitally via URI - no physical copies needed
ABC (Academic Bank of Credits) integration for education records

whoCanApply: Any Indian citizen with an Aadhaar number
Minors can register with guardian's Aadhaar
Organizations and government departments can register as issuers/requesters
whoCannotApply: Those without Aadhaar (Aadhaar is mandatory for sign-up)
NRIs without an active Indian Aadhaar number
Foreign nationals (Indian Aadhaar required)

documentsRequired: Mobile number linked to Aadhaar (for OTP verification)
Alternatively: Sign in via Parichay (government SSO) for government employees
howToApply: Visit digilocker.gov.in and sign up with Aadhaar
Download DigiLocker app (Android/iOS)
Verify with Aadhaar OTP
Fetch documents from issuing agencies automatically
schemes.grievance: support@digilocker.gov.in or in-app feedback

schemes.name: PDS / Ration Card
schemes.fullName: Public Distribution System / National Food Security Act
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
schemes.whatItIs: Subsidized food grain distribution to eligible households through a network of Fair Price Shops. Under NFSA, covers ~81 crore people (about 67% of population) with rice at Rs 3/kg, wheat at Rs 2/kg, and coarse grains at Rs 1/kg.
benefits: Priority Household (PHH): 5 kg per person per month of rice/wheat/coarse grains
Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY): 35 kg per household per month
Highly subsidized prices: Rice Rs 3/kg, Wheat Rs 2/kg, Coarse grains Rs 1/kg
PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY): Free 5 kg/person additional (extended periodically)
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC): Use ration card at any FPS across India
Sugar at subsidized rates in some states

whoCanApply: Priority Households (PHH): Based on SECC 2011 or state-specific criteria
Antyodaya (AAY): Poorest of the poor - landless laborers, marginal farmers, elderly, disabled, destitute, primitive tribes
Eligibility criteria vary by state (income ceiling, social category)
All Below Poverty Line (BPL) families
whoCannotApply: Above Poverty Line (APL) families in most states
Families exceeding state-specific income limits
Families with government employment and income above threshold

documentsRequired: Aadhaar card of all family members
Marriage certificate (for new family after marriage)
howToApply: Apply at State Food/Civil Supplies Department office
Online through state food portal (varies by state)
CSC centres for online application
Mera Ration app for ONORC portability

stateHelplines.note: Other states: contact district Food & Civil Supplies office or visit nfsa.gov.in

schemes.checkStatus: State food portal / nfsa.gov.in for NFSA status / Mera Ration app
schemes.grievance: FPS → Block Supply Officer → District Supply Officer → State Food Commission → Central government

schemes.name: PM Matru Vandana Yojana
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (earlier: Maternity Benefit Programme)
schemes.whatItIs: Maternity benefit providing cash incentive for pregnant and lactating women for the first two living children, to partially compensate wage loss and improve health-seeking behavior during pregnancy.
benefits: First child: Rs 5,000 in 3 installments (Rs 1,000 + Rs 2,000 + Rs 2,000)
Second child (if girl): Rs 6,000 in 2 installments
Installments linked to: registration, at least one ANC visit, child birth registration + first cycle vaccination
Total with JSY (Janani Suraksha Yojana) benefit: Up to Rs 6,000+ for first child
Direct Benefit Transfer to bank/post office account

whoCanApply: Pregnant women and lactating mothers for first two living children
Must be registered at Anganwadi Centre (AWC) or approved health facility
Must have Aadhaar-linked bank account
Must complete required ante-natal check-ups
whoCannotApply: Women in regular employment with Central/State government or PSU
Women already receiving similar maternity benefits under any other law
For third and subsequent pregnancies

documentsRequired: Copy of child birth certificate (for third installment)
howToApply: Register at nearest Anganwadi Centre (AWC) or Sub-Centre/PHC
Fill application form (Form 1-A for first installment)
Online: pmmvy.wcd.gov.in (CAS portal, filled by ASHA/ANM/AWW)
Applications usually submitted through ASHA worker or ANM
schemes.checkStatus: Through Anganwadi worker or pmmvy.wcd.gov.in CAS portal
schemes.grievance: Anganwadi worker → CDPO → District Programme Officer → State WCD

schemes.name: Samagra Shiksha
schemes.fullName: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of School Education & Literacy)
schemes.whatItIs: Integrated scheme for school education covering pre-school to Class XII. Merged three earlier schemes (SSA, RMSA, TE) into one umbrella programme for improving school education quality, access, and equity.
benefits: Free textbooks and uniforms for all children in government schools
Annual school grant: Rs 5,000-50,000 per school for maintenance
Composite school grant for libraries, sports, science labs
Free transport / transport allowance for children in remote areas
Inclusive education: Rs 3,500/child for children with special needs
Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV) for girls in educationally backward blocks
Teacher training and professional development
ICT labs and digital education support

whoCanApply: All children aged 6-18 in government and government-aided schools
Special focus: Girls, SC/ST, minority, children with special needs (CWSN)
Out-of-school children for mainstreaming
Teachers in government schools (for training components)
whoCannotApply: Private unaided school students (most components)
Generally benefits flow to schools/states, not individual applications

documentsRequired: Aadhaar card of child (for DBT components)
howToApply: Benefits flow through school system - no individual application usually needed
KGBV admission: Apply through district education office
Out-of-school children: Contact Block Education Officer / cluster resource person
Implementation through State/UT education departments

helpline.phone: 011-23765609 (MHRD helpline, Department of School Education & Literacy)

stateHelplines.note: Implemented by State Project Directors (SPDs) in each state. Contact your district Block Education Office or State Education Department. Key state helplines:

schemes.grievance: School → Block Education Officer → District Education Officer → State Project Director

schemes.name: Skill India / PMKVY
schemes.fullName: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (Skill India Mission)
schemes.whatItIs: Flagship skill training scheme enabling Indian youth to take industry-relevant skill training and get certified. Free short-term training (200-600 hours) with placement assistance, or recognition of prior learning for existing skills.
benefits: Free skill training at authorized PMKVY training centres
Training duration: 200-600 hours (2-6 months) for various trades
Assessment and certification by Sector Skill Councils
Placement assistance and post-training support
Reward: Rs 500-1,500 per candidate on successful certification
Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL): Certify existing skills without full training
Special focus: Industry 4.0, AI, IoT, drones, coding, 3D printing (PMKVY 4.0)
On-the-job training (OJT) component with stipend

whoCanApply: Indian youth (school/college dropouts or unemployed) seeking skill training
Minimum age: Varies by course (typically 15-45 years)
Aadhaar card mandatory
RPL: Workers with existing skills but no formal certification
PMKVY 4.0: Focus on new-age skills, green jobs, industry partnerships
whoCannotApply: Generally no exclusions - scheme is open to all eligible youth
Some courses have minimum education requirements (8th/10th/12th pass)

documentsRequired: Educational certificates (if applicable for the course)
howToApply: Find training centres: skillindia.gov.in
Visit PMKVY authorized training centre directly
Online registration on Skill India Digital portal
Through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)
Jan Seva Kendra / CSC for assistance
schemes.checkStatus: Skill India Digital portal / Training centre
schemes.grievance: Training centre → PMKVY district coordinator → State Skill Development Mission → NSDC
